record.paper_title: Quantum Communication: From Fundamentals to Recent Trends, Challenges and Open Problems
record.context_brief: multi-hop quantum routing metrics and algorithms
record.original_question: How should routes be selected in multi-hop quantum networks when route cost must account for entanglement-swapping time, fidelity, throughput, entangled-resource consumption, delay, resource competition, and waiting times, and when important quantum routing metrics are non-additive so classical shortest-path algorithms such as raw Dijkstra cannot be used directly?

evidence.quote: One important point that needs to be addressed here is how to find the route between the source to destination, in the presence of multiple hops between them.

The optimal route for the quantum routing algorithms is defined in [181] as the path that has the largest number of end-to-end entangled states in a time slot, the highest fidelity, the lowest consumption of entangled resources, and the shortest delay. Note that, for a quantum network with mesh topology, a single route that satisfies all these conditions is difficult to attain.

If the route costs (or inversely, the throughput) are defined using the metrics above (Eqn. 50), then the cost of the entire route is different from the sum of the costs of individual route. In other words, the route cost is not additive. Thus, the raw version of Dijkstra’s routing algorithm cannot be used directly.

The current routing challenges lie in finding improved quantum network models and appropriate routing metrics, designing better routing protocols, handling resource competition, and developing improved methods for calculating waiting times.

artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research articles (2020–2024) on entanglement routing—including comprehensive surveys, extended Dijkstra-type algorithms for non-additive monotonic metrics, concurrent entanglement routing schemes, and reinforcement-learning approaches—propose partial solutions for restricted versions of the problem, but no single framework is known that simultaneously and provably handles entanglement-swapping time, fidelity, throughput, resource consumption, delay, resource competition, and waiting times. The problem of fully general multi-criteria, non-additive multi-hop quantum routing remains an active open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Entanglement Routing in Quantum Networks: A Comprehensive Survey
status_evidence.snippet: Entanglement routing consists of choosing the optimal sequence of short-range entanglements... a quantum routing protocol must take into account the requested entanglement fidelity, the probabilistic nature of swapping operations, and the short lifetime of entangled states.
status_evidence.claim: Multi-criteria entanglement routing remains an active and only partially addressed research area.

status_evidence.title: Concurrent Entanglement Routing for Quantum Networks: Model and Designs
status_evidence.snippet: Extended Dijkstra's Algorithm (EDA) to find the best path... for any non-additive but monotonic routing metric.
status_evidence.claim: Partial solutions exist via extended Dijkstra-type algorithms for restricted non-additive monotonic metrics, but not for the full multi-objective setting.

status_evidence.title: Optimal routing and end-to-end entanglement distribution in quantum networks
status_evidence.snippet: Optimal routing and end-to-end entanglement distribution in quantum networks (2024).
status_evidence.claim: Optimal routing under all the listed quantum metrics simultaneously is still being investigated as of 2024.
